doc.title: Mr. and Mrs. A.C. Synigal and B. Bozant Interview, 1962-05-17
doc.interviewee: Mr. and Mrs. A.C. Synigal and B. Bozant

title: From block festivals to soiree dansants in club halls
summary: Square dancing by the Holy Family Sisters, rain ending the street festivals, and the move of the soiree to club halls.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Dance halls, lake resorts and where bands played

blocks.x: Well, we certainly would like to get that. Well, and they'd dance in the street. And then the Holy Family Sisters would come with their children and have the square dance. The sisters would come themselves and sit out on the porch here and they'll bring a band, a record. I think it was a record. And they'd get out in the street and they're right there in front of the door there. This is the headquarters for the fiesta. And they'd get out and dance, the square dance, at these block festivals. Now, that went on for several years until we got rained out. It rained for two years and we couldn't do anything. So, we decided not to be in the street anymore. So, after the block festival, then we went on to have the soiree dancin. That's right. And that was in the hall. In Autopilot. Autopilot hall. And that was nice. That was nice to have. It was French. And the people enjoyed that so much. So much. And after that, we had that at the Autopilot club. The soiree dancin. They were at the Autopilot club. Then we went on to the Wonderful Boys, let's name their homes.
We did because we couldn't get the Autopilot for that night. There was a mix up in the dates.
So, we went to the Wonderful Boys home. But you are not mirror, ma'am. Not mirror.

But usually, the soiree is just like we said before with the quadrille. You know, it's some parts that you really let your hand out. But the soiree dancin, we call it, that's our good time night. But of course, in a wonderful way. Because people come out to watch. I mean, it's a lot of fun. It really is. But in a nice way, of course. And then we have the tea.
